statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 15 of 100 in the low band, ten points below the 25 block threshold, while stress is extreme at 81 and confidence high at 89.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The named danger window spans the 12:30 UTC August consumer price report, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 14:00 UTC preliminary Michigan release, where the conditional path peaks at WATCH without reaching the block threshold.
headline: NQ trades 29,324.75, up 0.65%, holding about fifteen points beneath a 29,339.75 session high that extended only six points this hour, while VIX makes a fresh session low at 17.07, the 10-year eases to 4.943% and WTI falls back below $100, leaving tail at 15 and stress extreme at 81 roughly two hours before the 12:30 UTC August consumer price report.
body:
The new evidence this hour narrows rather than extends the overnight advance. NQ trades 29,324.75 on one feed and 29,321.75 on a second, up about 0.65% against a 29,135.25 previous close. Both feeds agree the session high is 29,339.75, which is only some six points above the 29,334.00 top recorded an hour ago. Against the 29,040.50 overnight low the band is roughly 299 points, and price now sits about fifteen points under the high rather than the forty points recorded previously.

That combination is the hour's central question. The forty-point retracement described an hour ago was bought back, and price has returned to the top of the range without producing a meaningful new high. Holding within fifteen points of a session extreme is a genuine tail amplifier and is why tail rises a point to 15. It stops there because the amplifier remains isolated and because the structure that actually defines tail risk, repeated extension after failed retracements, is absent: one pullback was recovered and the high advanced by six points, which describes a coil beneath resistance rather than a one-way path denying mean reversion.

The cross-asset picture continues to argue against alignment, and on two channels it has moved further away from it. VIX is 17.11, down 4.09%, and has printed a fresh session low of 17.07 inside a 17.07 to 17.71 band. A volatility index setting session lows while the index sits near session highs is the signature of an orderly drift rather than the violent directional repricing tail is built to capture. The ten-year yield is 4.943%, fractionally lower on the day and at the bottom of a 4.936% to 4.978% range, having been reported approaching 4.96% earlier this morning after an under-subscribed Treasury buyback operation. The two-year is 4.558%, up under a basis point and below its own 4.583% high.

The largest single change since the previous assessment is in energy. WTI has fallen 3.36% to $99.03, back below the $100 level it reclaimed on Thursday, and Brent is down 3.70% to $103.64. Both benchmarks settled far higher on Thursday, WTI at $102.48 and Brent at $107.63, and Brent was still quoted near $107.86 in European commentary earlier this morning. Crude giving back close to four percent intraday is a direct reduction in the inflation impulse behind the entire rate-hike narrative, and it arrives two hours before the inflation print that narrative depends on. Brent nonetheless remains roughly nine percent higher on the week, so this is a correction within an elevated regime rather than a resolution of it.

Stress eases one point to 81 and stays in the extreme band on that oil and volatility correction. The underlying environment is unchanged in substance. A global bond selloff has carried the ten-year toward 5% with the long end pressured by heavy supply, crude remains above $100 on the unresolved Strait of Hormuz conflict, and the three major U.S. averages fell for a fourth consecutive session on Thursday, the Dow down 0.6%, the S&P 500 down 0.58% and the Nasdaq Composite down 0.65%, leaving the week firmly negative. Market pricing for the 16 September decision implies roughly a 69% chance of a move, up sharply from a week earlier. That is precisely the difficult, high-volatility environment stress is designed to describe, and under this framework it is scored independently of the price-path question.

One sector input continues to support the overnight bid. TSMC's filed August revenue of NT$514.81 billion, up 10.1% on the month and 53.3% on the year, is a record month and the first above NT$500 billion, driven by artificial-intelligence demand that has kept advanced capacity fully booked. Thursday's U.S. semiconductor session was negative, so this remains a catalyst the last cash close did not fully reflect.

The August consumer price report at 12:30 UTC is the final inflation input before the decision, with consensus near 3.4% headline year-on-year and 2.4% to 2.5% core. It is a checkpoint, not an automatic block. Its importance and the dispersion around it are carried in stress and confidence, and tail will be revised on the observed post-release path rather than on the magnitude of any surprise. The conditional forecast therefore peaks at 23 in the release slot and 22 across the cash open, both inside the watch band and beneath the 25 block threshold, then decays through the afternoon on the assumption that retracements continue to be granted.

Confidence holds at 89. Two independent live NQ feeds agree on the session high, real-time VIX and two-year and ten-year yields are current, both crude benchmarks are current, the seven-day calendar is verified against a primary calendar source, and every material story referenced here was confirmed by direct retrieval. The shared cross-asset context file was both outside its ninety-minute freshness window and flagged as a partial collection at this assessment time, so it was not used; this assessment rests entirely on independently fetched live evidence.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 10:00 UTC on 10 September to 09:00 UTC on 11 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 11 with the mode recorded as mixed through the European morning. The single excursion sits in the middle of the U.S. session: tail 14 at 11:00 UTC as the mode turned trend-down on the pre-release grind, 20 at 12:00 UTC when the August producer price report printed and the mode became event/whipsaw, and the window peak of 24 at 13:00 UTC across the cash open with the mode back to trend-down. Those two slots are the only ones mapped to WATCH and neither reached the 25 block threshold. Tail then decayed as price discovery stayed orderly, easing to 17 by 14:00 UTC and holding 14 to 19 through the afternoon, with event/whipsaw recorded again at 20:00 and 21:00 UTC around the cash close. From 22:00 UTC the overnight session normalised into an 11 to 15 band with mixed conditions, and the final four slots at 06:00, 07:00, 08:00 and 09:00 UTC record trend-up at tail 13, 14, 13 and 14 as the overnight advance extended and was then bought back. Stress never left the extreme band, running 82 to 87 across the whole window, and confidence held 84 to 89 throughout.
outlookSummary: The forward window covers the rest of the 11 September session and ends inside the CME weekend closure that begins at 21:00 UTC. Conditional tail starts at 15 on the observed hold within fifteen points of the session high and stays at 15 through the final pre-release hour, where thinning quoted depth is a positioning effect rather than observed structure. The window peak is 23 in the 12:00 UTC slot containing the August consumer price report, inside the watch band and below the 25 block threshold, and 22 in the 13:00 UTC slot spanning the cash open where a post-event move is either confirmed or rejected. The 14:00 UTC slot carrying the preliminary Michigan release eases to 19 on the assumption that price discovery is orderly by then. The afternoon decays through 17, 16 and 15, holds 15 across the budget statement, lifts to 16 into the final pre-close hour and 18 across the 20:00 UTC cash close where weekly positioning concentrates, then falls to a 5 to 6 floor for the closure hours that represents residual gap risk into the Sunday reopen rather than any intraday mechanism. Two slots are mapped to WATCH and none reaches the block threshold. Stress stays extreme through the U.S. session, peaking at 92 in the release slot, and decays into the elevated band across the weekend. Confidence eases from 89 to around 68 as the horizon moves past the last observable quote.
